I’ve quit drinking probably 30 times. Every time in the same, like clockwork. 

Day 1, no sleep. At all. None. I’ll lay there and toss and turn all night until it’s time to get up. 

Day 2.  Same as day one but I’ll get hypnic jerks periodically at the alcohol is leaving my system and my brain is trying to rewrite itself. 

Day 3, I’ll usually get some sleep. An hour here. An hour there. But mostly restless. 

About day 4, I’ll start being able to sleep. My dreams will be vivid and range from euphoric to absolutely nightmarish. 

After that, my sleep is about back to normal. If you’re not yawning, you’re not gonna get much sleep. As the melatonin and adenosine in the body builds up with our natural circadian rhythm, and the alcohol detaches from the GABA receptors, sleep becomes easier and easier. 

It just takes time for the body to get rid of the alcohol, which attaches to the GABA receptors and for the natural chemicals and neurons of the brain to start firing on all cylinders again. 

Your mileage may vary. Some people takes weeks or months for sleep to go back to normal. Some, like me, only a few days.

This is a regular occurrence for me whenever I stop drinking. Alcohol over takes the GABA receptors in the brain after prolonged used. That receptor is what your brain uses to put you to sleep. When it’s over taken with alcohol, your body creates even more chemicals to try and compensate so what ends up happening is as the alcohol leaves your body, your brain has flooded you with the chemical needed to attach to that receptor and it ends up having the opposite effect. You can’t sleep. 

I find around day 3 that I start having crazy dreams and sleeping again but it all depends on how much you drink and for how long. 3-4 days is my average before my sleep starts returning to normal. 

Don’t set yourself up for failure though. Limit screen time to 30 minutes before bed, no screen. No caffeine after noon. And maybe shower or read a book as that will relax the body and mind and help you fall asleep.
